fact: The Namibian reports a N$40m contract awarded in June 2026 to 6th Grain Corporation to deploy an AI and satellite-imagery crop-monitoring system for the agriculture ministry, which the government terminated in August 2026 as not meeting legal and procedural requirements.
system: AI and satellite imagery-driven crop monitoring system

fact: The agriculture ministry signed a one-year N$39.5 million contract with 6th Grain Corporation to introduce satellite imagery and AI to monitor staple crops, forecast crops and assess drought (Windhoek Observer, citing the ministry and US Embassy).
Through the Science Granting Councils Initiative the NCRST has funded projects on AI-powered tools for early disease detection, per the NCRST authors citing SGCI 2024.

NASA Harvest says its AI and machine-learning team built a high-resolution national cropland mask for Namibia, provided to the Ministry of Agriculture, Water and Land Reform under a pilot to better target monitoring and assessments.

Health Minister Esperance Luvindao said Namibia has introduced AI-powered digital chest X-ray technology for tuberculosis screening and early diagnosis, and that she was screened with it at a World TB Day event in Omusati.

Two AI tutoring labs were launched on 21 September 2026 at Angra Pequena Senior Secondary School, a government school in Luderitz, where all 436 learners can access personalised tutoring and the 20 teachers have teaching-assistant support; YYeni AI says the programme was already operating before the launch, funded by BW Kudu and Namport.
system: AI tutoring labs (Project Aristotle, YYeni AI)
